summary: I reviewed the review instructions, the file list, the watcher code, the vendored debouncer patch, the paging code in the MCP server, and the bubblewrap sandbox used by the evaluator. I found one concrete watcher defect: the new directory-race retry handles only one of the two race windows. Watch registration fails when a directory is deleted after its watch succeeds but before the walk reads its contents. It also fails on a second race in one pass. A registration failure makes every indexed read return an error until a retry succeeds, and at startup it makes the watcher fail to start. The paging code in the MCP server and the debouncer patch matched their documented behavior. The 152,000-line bundle is too large for a full review in one pass, so most of the semantic code (queries.rs, reference_report.rs, edit_check/*, test_commands.rs) and the eval result files were not reviewed line by line.

findings.title: Watch registration fails when a directory is deleted during the walk, after its watch succeeds
findings.body: `synchronize_registrations` retries the walk only when `debouncer.watch(&path)` fails and `metadata(&path)` reports NotFound (watcher.rs:528-543). A directory can also be deleted after `watch` succeeds but before the `ignore` walker reads it. In that case the walker returns an I/O NotFound error for that directory. Line 510 (`result.map_err(WatcherError::Ignore)?`) passes that error up with no retry. Also, line 538 returns an error on the second race in one pass (`directory_race_retries > 0`), so two short-lived directories in one walk also fail. Build tools and test runners often create and delete such directories in folders that are not ignored. The results: (1) at startup, `watcher_worker` sends the error and `start_watcher` fails (lines 320-322); (2) during a reconcile, `record_registration_failure` sets a failure that `clear_failure_if_unchanged` cannot clear (lines 131, 639-644). Every indexed read then returns an error until the backoff retry succeeds, with a wait of 1 s that doubles up to 30 s. The only regression test, `registration_rewalks_when_a_discovered_directory_disappears` (lines 1099-1128), deletes the directory before `watch`. It does not test a deletion after `watch` succeeds, or two races in one pass.
findings.recommendation: When a walk error is an I/O NotFound for a path under the root, and that path no longer exists, treat it like the existing race case: rewalk, or skip the entry and let the next generation drop its stale watch. Allow a small number of race retries per pass instead of one. Add a test that deletes a directory after its `watch` call succeeds, and a test with two races in one pass.

next_steps: Fix the walk-error race in `synchronize_registrations` and add tests for a deletion after `watch` succeeds and for two races in one pass.
Review the semantic code that changed (queries.rs, reference_report.rs, edit_check/*, test_commands.rs) in smaller parts. This pass did not cover it line by line.
Check the evaluator scripts (edit_evaluation.py, completed_edit_campaign.py, edit_snapshot.py) against the result files. This pass read only edit_sandbox.py.

evidence.observation: Any walker error, including NotFound for a directory deleted during the walk, goes up through `?` at line 510 with no retry.
The retry runs only when `watch()` fails and the path is gone. It allows one retry per pass; a second race returns an error.
At startup, a registration error makes the watcher worker exit, so `start_watcher` fails.
`clear_failure_if_unchanged` will not clear a registration failure, so indexed reads keep returning an error until a registration retry succeeds.
The registration retry uses backoff from 1 s up to 30 s, so a single race can block reads for a long time.
The regression test deletes the directory only before `watch()`. It does not test a deletion after `watch()` succeeds, or two races in one pass.
The backported remove handling replaces the path's queue with the removal event and drops child queues. This matches PATCH.md.
The offset and limit checks reject a limit above 200 and an offset+limit overflow. This matches the documented paging rules.
